elements_selected.content: Implement section-level drift detection per REQ-043a. Drift detection runs during zetl check after the scanner has produced current Merkle trees. Algorithm (from §6.5): for each SPL block in the current scan, compare: 1) current section grounding hash (freshly computed) vs cached section grounding hash (from theory.json spl_blocks), 2) current SPL AST hash (freshly computed) vs cached SPL AST hash. If section grounding hash changed AND SPL AST hash unchanged → section drift detected. Severity: Warning if immediately-adjacent leaves changed (leaves at section_start or section_end-1 are non-SPL and differ), Info if only distant leaves changed. The DriftDiagnostic includes: file, spl_line, DriftType::SectionDrift { section_heading }, severity, message per the CON-019 example. Drift requires a prior theory build to compare against — if no theory.json exists, skip drift detection (no baseline). Implement as detect_section_drift(current: &FileMerkle, cached_theory: &TheoryCache) -> Vec<DriftDiagnostic> in src/drift.rs (new) or src/merkle.rs.
